items.title: Drive a robot with one forearm
items.text:
A Myo armband reads your arm like a lever: its angle sets speed and steering, and a firm fist brakes.

Drive it See the deck Open the sim

items.title: What we built
items.text:
Our team's entry to the AWARE-AI Fall Hackathon at RIT, October 22-23, 2026. Every team got the same browser sim of a Clearpath Jackal, a command bridge and a Myo armband. The task: turn the armband's signals into forward speed and turn rate, drive three timed courses, then keep the robot drivable over a slow, lossy link.

We started with five muscle gestures and a classifier, and it broke as soon as the forearm rolled. So the controller steers with the armband's motion sensor, which rolling cannot fool, and keeps the muscle signal for one job: a deliberate fist that brakes. A lidar assist slows before obstacles and nudges you through a gate you are already aimed at.

items.title: What it did
items.text:
20.7 s L1 Gates, median of 4 runs, 0 collisions

26.6 s L2 Slalom, median of 6 runs, 0 collisions

16.3 s L3 Corridor + Dock, median of 4 runs, 0 collisions

All 51 recorded runs finished with no missed gates. A new driver calibrates in about 2.5 minutes with one command. All the results, including what did not work →

items.title: The team
items.text: AJ Barea, Jose, Kiran and Xinyi Liu. Xinyi built the gate assist and the sim's lidar minimap; AJ wrote the lever controller, the neural-network study and the deck generator. The sim, the bridge and the event kit come from the organizers' AHRTLab/Hackathon repo, which ours forks.

items.title: Design brief
items.text: Copied from AHRTLab/IEEE-telepresence-shared-control/docs/JACKAL_HACKATHON_BRIEF.md. In this repo the platform (protocol/, web/, bridge/, models/) sits at the root, and the event material (starter kit, guide, presentations) lives at the root of AHRTLab/Hackathon (main = the current event; past events are branches) instead of a separate new repo (brief §13).

items.title: AWARE-AI Hackathon: Jackal Sim + Command Bridge
Project Brief & Implementation Spec
items.text: Input for the implementation plan. It records decisions, constraints, interfaces, and known risks. It is not the plan itself; the plan (file-by-file tasks) is produced from this. Sibling project for patterns and reusable code: AHRTLab/IEEE-telepresence-shared-control (see its docs/BRIEF.md, docs/SPIKE_FINDINGS.md, web/extras/logger.ts, web/extras/rtlx.ts, web/deploy.sh, and the Playwright *_test.mjs files).

items.title: 1. Context & goal
items.text:
• Event: AWARE-AI hackathon. (TBD: date, duration, number of teams, team size, participant background.)
  • Lead: Jamison Heard (RIT, AHRT Lab).
  • Goal: Teams build their own human-input controller (Myo EMG/IMU, joystick, keyboard, anything else) for a Clearpath Jackal in a browser MuJoCo simulation. The only requirement: their controller emits commands that follow one fixed command contract (Section 3). The sim, the bridge, and every team's controller are developed and tested independently against that contract.
  • Design principle: the contract mirrors ROS geometry_msgs/Twist (linear.x, angular.z) so the same commands can later drive the physical lab Jackal (ROS Noetic, jackal_velocity_controller on /cmd_vel) with no change on the team's side (Section 8, stretch).

items.title: 2. System overview
items.text:
[team controller]                    [bridge, Python, localhost]                [browser sim]
  Myo / gamepad / EMG    --LSL-->   ingress: LSL | UDP | WebSocket     --WS-->   MuJoCo-WASM Jackal
  classifier / script    --UDP-->   validate, select active source,              course + scoring
                         --WS--->   rate-limit, forward                <--WS--   state @ 20 Hz
                                    egress: browser WS, LSL outlets,
                                            (stretch) ROS /cmd_vel
  • Everything runs on one laptop per team by default: controller, bridge, and Chrome tab.
  • The browser page is a static site (GitHub Pages) that connects to ws://localhost:8765.
  • Without a bridge, the page falls back to keyboard + Gamepad API so it is always drivable.

items.title: 3. The command contract (the most important section; freeze early)
items.text: Version this as protocol/v1. Ship a JSON Schema in protocol/cmd.schema.json and protocol/state.schema.json, plus protocol/PROTOCOL.md for students.

items.title: 3.1 Command (controller to sim)
items.text:
JSON over WebSocket or UDP:

{"type": "cmd", "v": 0.4, "w": -0.8, "estop": false, "action": null,
 "source": "team3-myo", "seq": 1042, "t": 1739.214}
Field Type Req Meaning type "cmd" yes Message kind v float, m/s yes Forward speed (body x). Positive = forward w float, rad/s yes Yaw rate (body z). Positive = counter-clockwise (left) estop bool no (false) Latched stop until a {"type":"reset"} or UI button action string or null no Discrete event: e.g. "horn", "mark", "mode:<name>". Logged, shown in HUD source string no Free-form id, shown in HUD and logged seq int no Sender sequence number (lets the sim count drops) t float, s no Sender clock; echoed back for latency measurement

LSL form of the same command (for teams already in LSL): - Stream name JackalCmd, type Control, 2 channels float32 [v, w], any nominal rate (0 = irregular is fine). - Optional stream name JackalAction, type Markers, 1 channel string: estop, reset, or any action string.

items.title: 3.2 Rules the sim enforces (authoritative; the bridge enforces the same as defense in depth)
items.text:
• Clamp: |v| <= V_MAX, |w| <= W_MAX. Sim defaults V_MAX = 2.0 m/s, W_MAX = 4.0 rad/s (Jackal spec; verify against jackal_control/config/control.yaml). Course configs may lower these.
  • Acceleration limit: rate-limit applied v, w (configurable; default about 2.0 m/s^2, 6.0 rad/s^2, tune for feel). Applied values are reported in state.
  • Deadman: no valid command for 250 ms means the target goes to zero (decelerate under the accel limit). HUD shows DEADMAN. Students will unplug things; this must never fail.
  • Rate: accept up to 100 Hz; apply latest-wins once per control tick (50 Hz).
  • Invalid messages (schema fail, NaN, inf) are dropped and counted, never applied.

items.title: 3.3 State (sim to controllers), 20 Hz
items.text:
Available on the bridge WebSocket (ws://localhost:8765/state) and as LSL outlets, so teams can build closed-loop or assistive controllers (shared autonomy, collision avoidance, gate guidance):

{"type": "state", "t": 12.35, "pose": {"x": 1.2, "y": -0.4, "yaw": 0.31},
 "vel": {"v": 0.38, "w": -0.75}, "cmd_applied": {"v": 0.4, "w": -0.8}, "cmd_echo_t": 1739.214,
 "status": "ok", "collisions": 2,
 "scan": {"angle_min": -2.356, "angle_inc": 0.02618, "range_max": 10.0, "ranges": [ ... 180 floats ... ]},
 "course": {"id": "L1-gates", "next_gate": 3, "gates_passed": 2, "elapsed": 12.35, "done": false}}
  • status is one of ok | deadman | estop | idle | finished.
  • scan is a simulated 2D planar lidar (180 beams over 270 degrees, chassis height). It stands in for the real robot's Velodyne in a simplified form.

LSL outlets published by the bridge: - JackalState, type State, float32 channels [x, y, yaw, v, w, v_cmd, w_cmd, collisions], 20 Hz. - JackalScan, type Range, 180 float32 channels, 20 Hz. - JackalEvents, type Markers, strings: run_start, gate:<k>, collision, deadman, estop, finish, action:<x>. Lets LabRecorder save EMG + robot state + task events time-synced in one XDF, which is the point of using LSL for AWARE-AI.

items.title: 4. Simulation (web/, static site, what students open)
4.1 Stack decision
items.text:
• Vite + TypeScript + three.js + official MuJoCo WASM (@mujoco/mujoco, single-threaded build), so no COOP/COEP headers are needed and GitHub Pages works.
  • Do not use mjswan here. mjswan's value in the telepresence project was the ONNX policy pipeline; this project has no policy, and mjswan required patching its generated runtime to inject control. A hand-written step loop with the WebSocket input is simpler. Known glue costs (asset VFS writes, MuJoCo Z-up vs three.js Y-up, quaternion order) are modest for one robot plus primitive obstacles.
  • Fallback if the official bindings block something: mjswan 0.8.0 with a vendored template.

items.title: 4.2 Jackal model
items.text:
• No Jackal in MuJoCo Menagerie (verify). Convert jackal_description (Clearpath, BSD; verify license) URDF to MJCF with a scripted, reproducible converter (models/jackal/convert.py); simplify collision to boxes and cylinders; keep the STL meshes for visuals.
  • Key dimensions to verify from the URDF: chassis about 0.508 x 0.430 x 0.25 m, about 17 kg, wheel radius about 0.098 m, track about 0.376 m.
  • Optional visual-only payload to match the lab robot (lidar puck, arm in retract). No arm control.

items.title: 4.3 Drive model (decision)
items.text:
• Default: kinematic base. Chassis on planar joints (slide x, slide y, hinge yaw) with velocity actuators; each tick set targets from applied (v, w) rotated into the world frame. Obstacles still collide and block the robot. Wheels spin for visuals only. Rationale: skid-steer contact friction is notoriously finicky in physics sims (the lab already hit this in Isaac, needing an inflated wheelDistance); the hackathon cannot depend on it.
  • Stretch: "physics mode" toggle. Free-joint chassis + 4 wheel velocity actuators with differential mixing; documented friction parameters. Lets advanced teams feel real skid-steer behavior.

items.title: 4.4 Page features
items.text:
• Connection panel: bridge URL (default ws://localhost:8765/sim, overridable by ?bridge= URL param), status light, active source, message rate, drops, round-trip latency from t echo.
  • HUD: applied v/w bars, status (ok/deadman/estop), last action, timer, gates, collisions.
  • Cameras: chase (default), top-down, onboard first-person. FPV is the hard "telepresence" view.
  • Fallback input: keyboard (W/S v, A/D w, Space stop) and Gamepad API, used only when no bridge source is active. Bridge input always wins when present.
  • Run controls: course picker, Start, Reset, E-stop, Clear E-stop, team id field, CSV download.
  • Optional AWARE-AI knobs (cheap, high value): injected command latency (0 to 1000 ms), packet drop percentage, and a post-run NASA-RTLX form (reuse rtlx.ts). Lets teams study how their interface degrades under telepresence conditions.

items.title: 4.5 Courses (web/public/courses/*.json)
items.text:
Data-driven so staff can add courses without code: arena size, walls, obstacles (box/cylinder), ordered gates (two posts each), start pose, finish zone, time limit, optional speed caps.

Id Course Tests L0 Sandbox Open arena, no scoring; for bring-up L1 Gates 6 to 8 wide gates in open field; basic steering L2 Slalom Tight alternating gates; fine control of w L3 Corridor + dock Narrow corridor, then stop inside a box (within 0.15 m and 10 degrees) for 1 s; fine control of v and stopping L4 (stretch) Dynamic A moving obstacle or a goal only visible in scan; rewards closed-loop assistance

Scoring (shown at finish, logged): score_time = elapsed + 5 s per collision + 10 s per missed gate; DNF on timeout. Also log path length, mean |dw/dt| (smoothness), percent time in deadman, and command drop count.

items.title: 4.6 Logging
items.text:
• Per run: one CSV row (team, source, course, completed, elapsed, score_time, collisions, missed gates, path length, smoothness, deadman percent, drops, mean latency, latency/drop knob settings, RTLX).
  • Per tick: downloadable 20 Hz trace (CSV) of pose, applied and requested commands, status.
  • Client-side only. If data becomes research data, IRB applies (same note as the telepresence brief).

items.title: 5. Bridge (bridge/, Python, runs on each team laptop)
items.text:
• Single command: jackal-bridge (or python -m bridge). Python 3.10+, asyncio, websockets, pylsl, jsonschema. One requirements.txt; consider uv for fast installs.
  • Ingress adapters (all enabled by default):
  • LSL inlet: resolves JackalCmd (+ JackalAction).
  • UDP JSON on 127.0.0.1:9870 (easiest from MATLAB or any language).
  • WebSocket client endpoint ws://localhost:8765/cmd.
  • Egress: browser ws://localhost:8765/sim; state on ws://localhost:8765/state; LSL outlets (Section 3.3); stretch ROS adapter (Section 8).
  • Source arbitration: latest-wins from one active source. Active source = first to send after idle, or pinned via --source lsl|udp|ws. Switching requires the active source to go silent for 1 s (prevents two inputs fighting). Report active source to the browser.
  • Validation + clamping identical to Section 3.2 (shared constants generated from the schema, or one protocol/limits.json read by both TS and Python).
  • Console view: one-line live status (source, rate, last v/w, browser connected, LSL peers).
  • --loopback-test flag: sends a short scripted command sequence and checks state comes back, for quick "is my setup working" checks at the event.

items.title: 6. Starter kit for teams (examples/)
items.text:
Each example is short, commented, and runnable on its own:

File What it shows keyboard_teleop.py Minimal command sender (WebSocket) gamepad_teleop.py Joystick axes to (v, w) with deadzone and expo curve fake_myo_lsl.py Publishes synthetic 8-channel EMG (200 Hz) + IMU as LSL; lets teams build without hardware myo_lsl_publisher.py Real Myo to LSL (raw EMG + IMU). See risk 1 myo_emg_example.py Minimal read → feature → decide → send example. (The baseline myo_threshold_controller.py is staff-only, gitignored under staff/) state_listener.py Subscribes to state and prints pose, scan minimum, gate progress assist_example.py Shared-autonomy example: blends human (v, w) with a scan-based collision-avoidance term autopilot_gates.py Pure-pursuit through gates from state; reference solution and integration test controller_template.py def step(state, my_input) -> (v, w) skeleton with the plumbing done matlab/send_cmd.m UDP send snippet for MATLAB users

items.title: 7. Student-facing docs
items.text:
• docs/STUDENT_GUIDE.md (one page): install, run bridge, open URL, send your first command, read state, the rules (deadman, clamps, one active source), how scoring works, how to record with LabRecorder.
  • protocol/PROTOCOL.md: the contract, with copy-paste examples in Python, MATLAB, and JavaScript.
  • docs/RUNBOOK.md (staff): build, deploy, pre-event checklist, troubleshooting table.

items.title: 8. Real Jackal mode (stretch; not required for hackathon day)
items.text:
• Bridge --ros adapter publishes geometry_msgs/Twist to the Jackal (ROS Noetic) at 20 Hz. Run it where rospy exists (on the Jackal, or a Noetic Docker container with ROS_MASTER_URI pointed at the Jackal). Alternative: rosbridge + WebSocket.
  • Publish to a topic that the Jackal's twist_mux ranks below joystick teleop (verify topic names and priorities in the robot's twist_mux config), so the staff Xbox controller always overrides.
  • Safety in real mode: caps 0.5 m/s and 1.0 rad/s; deadman 250 ms enforced in the bridge; staff member holding the physical e-stop; cleared area; arm in retract with its teleop node idle.
  • Finale idea: the top team's controller drives the real robot through a taped-out L1 course.

items.title: 9. Non-goals
items.text: No RL training or ONNX policies. No multi-user shared sim. No 3D lidar or camera streams to teams (2D scan only). No arm control. No cloud backend.

items.title: 10. Known risks / open questions (resolve in the spike)
items.text:
1. [HIGH] Myo connectivity on event laptops. Myo is discontinued; Myo Connect/SDK support on current macOS/Windows is uncertain. Candidates: pyomyo (needs the Myo USB BLE dongle) or a direct BLE client via bleak. Test on the actual hackathon machines early; count working armbands and dongles. fake_myo_lsl.py keeps teams unblocked regardless.
  2. [MEDIUM] Chrome Local Network Access. An HTTPS GitHub Pages site connecting to ws://localhost should be allowed (localhost counts as a secure context), but recent Chrome versions may show a local-network permission prompt. Document "click Allow". Fallback: serve the site locally (npm run preview) over plain HTTP.
  3. [MEDIUM] Cross-machine setups. An HTTPS page cannot open plain ws:// to a LAN IP (mixed content). If a team splits devices, serve the site locally or run the bridge with TLS. Default guidance: everything on one laptop.
  4. [MEDIUM] LSL discovery on campus wifi. Multicast may be blocked on eduroam; same-machine streams work over loopback. For cross-machine LSL, use KnownPeers in lsl_api.cfg.
  5. [LOW] pylsl on macOS ARM. Recent pylsl wheels bundle liblsl (verify version); otherwise install liblsl via Homebrew/conda.
  6. [LOW] MuJoCo WASM raycasting for the scan. Confirm mj_ray/mj_multiRay are exposed in the JS bindings; 180 rays at 20 Hz is cheap either way.
  7. [LOW] First-load size on event wifi. MuJoCo WASM is about 9 MB; no onnxruntime this time. Pre-load on laptops before the event.

items.title: 11. Milestones
items.text: M Deliverable Done when M0 Spike Jackal MJCF loads in browser; kinematic drive by keyboard; L0 sandbox Robot drives and collides with a box in Chrome on a Mac M1 Bridge Bridge with LSL/UDP/WS ingress, browser egress, deadman, clamps, HUD connection panel keyboard_teleop.py and fake_myo_lsl.py both drive the sim; unplug test stops the robot M2 Courses L1 to L3, scoring, logging, CSV, cameras, state + scan + LSL outlets autopilot_gates.py completes L1 to L3 headlessly; XDF recording contains all streams M3 Starter kit All examples/, STUDENT_GUIDE.md, PROTOCOL.md A new user goes from clone to driving in under 10 minutes following only the guide M4 Polish Latency/drop knobs, RTLX, physics mode, deploy to GitHub Pages, RUNBOOK Live URL works on a clean Chrome profile with a local bridge M5 Stretch Real Jackal ROS adapter, L4 Staff-supervised drive of the lab Jackal from keyboard_teleop.py

items.title: 12. Acceptance tests (automate with Playwright + pytest, like the telepresence repo)
items.text:
1. Page loads, scene renders, no console errors.
  2. Bridge + scripted sender: v = 0.5 for 3 s moves the robot 1.2 to 1.6 m forward (accel limited).
  3. Deadman: stop sending; applied speed below 0.05 m/s within 400 ms.
  4. Clamp: send v = 10; applied v <= V_MAX. NaN and malformed JSON are dropped and counted.
  5. Arbitration: two sources sending; only the active one is applied until it goes silent for 1 s.
  6. autopilot_gates.py completes L1 and logs a CSV row with all fields from Section 4.6.
  7. LSL round trip: fake_myo_lsl.py to controller to JackalCmd to sim to JackalState is received by a test inlet.
  8. Fallback: with no bridge, keyboard drives the robot.

items.title: 13. Suggested repo layout (new repo, e.g. AHRTLab/aware-ai-jackal-sim)
items.text:
protocol/   cmd.schema.json  state.schema.json  limits.json  PROTOCOL.md
models/     jackal/ (MJCF, meshes, convert.py, LICENSE)
web/        Vite + TS app (src/sim, src/net, src/ui, src/courses), public/courses/*.json, tests/
bridge/     bridge package (ingress/, egress/, arbitration.py, cli.py), tests/
examples/   starter kit (Section 6), matlab/
docs/       STUDENT_GUIDE.md  RUNBOOK.md  BRIEF.md (this file)
scripts/    deploy.sh (adapt from the telepresence repo)

items.title: 14. Open decisions for the lead (fill in before planning)
items.text:
• Hackathon date, length, number of teams, team size, participants' programming background.
  • Event machines: student laptops (which OSes) or lab machines; how many Myos and dongles work.
  • Is the real Jackal finale in scope?
  • Public or private repo (student access, GitHub Pages hosting).
  • Whether RTLX and the latency/drop knobs are part of judging or just optional exploration.
  • Judging criteria beyond score time (creativity of interface, workload, accessibility).

items.title: 15. Workflow
items.text: This brief, then a detailed implementation plan in Claude Code (plan mode), then implementation milestone by milestone, each closed by its acceptance tests. Start with M0 + the contract files so teams' starter code can be written in parallel against protocol/v1.

items.title: Staff Runbook: AWARE-AI Jackal Hackathon
items.text: For organizers and TAs. Students use STUDENT_GUIDE.md; design notes and every quirk we hit are in SPIKE_FINDINGS.md.

items.title: 1. Deploying
items.text:
• The sim site (https://ahrtlab.github.io/Hackathon/) deploys itself. Every push to main runs .github/workflows/pages.yml, which runs the unit tests, builds, and publishes in about 2 minutes. Watch the repo's Actions tab. A red run means a test failed and the previous site stays live.
  • One-time repo setting: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions. If the site ever shows the README instead of the sim, this setting has been changed to "Deploy from a branch".
  • gh-pages = what is live. After each deploy the workflow commits the published files to the gh-pages branch, so its latest commit names the main commit that is live. Don't edit it by hand, and don't point Pages at it.
  • Courses: edit or add web/public/courses/*.json (format: web/public/courses/README.md; L1–L3 come from web/scripts/make_courses.py). npm test (and CI) fails if a course doesn't compile, starts in a collision, or can't be completed by the reference autopilot.
  • Staff-only material (the baseline myo_threshold_controller.py students must beat, its tests and calibration fixture) lives in staff/ (repo root), which is gitignored: it is never pushed and a fresh clone doesn't have it. Keep a private copy (lab drive or a private repo). Its e2e test skips itself where the folder is missing. Run its unit tests with pytest -q staff.
  • lsl-web-viewer is its own repo (https://github.com/AHRTLab/lsl-web-viewer). Releases are git tags; environment.yml here pins one (currently v0.2.0). To ship a viewer change, tag a new version there, push the tag, then update the pin.
  • Before an event: run everything locally once: 
    cd web && npm test && npm run e2e:chrome          # sim, bridge link, courses, knobs, RTLX
cd ../bridge && pytest -q
cd .. && pytest -q examples/tests

items.title: 2. Pre-event checklist (a day before)
items.text:
Every laptop (student or lab): - [ ] git clone https://github.com/AHRTLab/Hackathon.git, then conda env create -f environment.yml (or conda env update … --prune). - [ ] conda activate jackal && jackal-bridge --serve-site --open once while online. This caches the site (about 3 MB) so it also works offline. The page should load, and the top-left panel should turn amber. - [ ] python examples/keyboard_teleop.py drives the robot (panel turns green). - [ ] Pick L1, then run python examples/autopilot_gates.py. It should finish and print result: finish. - [ ] Macs: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Bluetooth: enable the terminal app students will use. - [ ] Google Chrome installed (the GitHub Pages link needs it; other browsers must use --serve-site). - [ ] If recording: LabRecorder installed.

Every Myo armband: - [ ] Charged (USB). Myo Connect quit on every laptop (it holds the armband). - [ ] python examples/myo_check.py connects, buzzes twice and shows the battery %. Label each armband with its address from step 2 of that output (useful when 10 are in one room).

items.title: 3. On the day
items.text:
Start order on each laptop (separate terminals, all conda activate jackal, all in Hackathon/): 1. jackal-bridge --serve-site --open: the sim opens. Pick the course. 2. The input: myo_lsl_publisher.py (real Myo) or fake_myo_lsl.py. Then lsl-web-viewer --open to check signals. 3. The team's controller (or myo_emg_example.py, keyboard_teleop.py, …).

Reading the sim page:

Where What it tells you Top-left light grey = no bridge · amber = bridge, nobody driving · green = driving (source + ingress shown) · "Another sim tab" = close the other tab HUD status pill OK · IDLE · DEADMAN (commands stopped for > 250 ms) · E-STOP (latched; Clear E-stop) HUD badge ⏱ 300 ms · 10 % drop a telepresence condition is active Top centre course, clock, gates, live score; the next gate glows yellow

Telepresence conditions (studies): set latency (0–1000 ms) and drop (0–50 %) in the controls panel, or put them in the URL so every run is identical: http://localhost:8765/Hackathon/?course=L1-gates&latency=300&drop=10&seed=1&rtlx=1. They apply to every input (bridge and keyboard). A change during a run waits for Reset, so each run has one condition. rtlx=1 turns on the NASA-RTLX form after each run.

Judging: the procedure (3 attempts per course on L1–L3, best counts, plus a degraded-link L1 run at ?course=L1-gates&latency=300&drop=10&seed=1) and the rubric are in RUBRIC.md. Enter each team's id on the page before their runs, and download the Runs CSV afterwards.

Collecting data at the end of a session: - Runs CSV (one row per run: time, score, collisions, missed gates, path, smoothness, deadman %, drops, latency, knob settings + seed, RTLX + subscales) and Last trace (20 Hz) from the page. These live in the browser tab only, so download them before closing it. - lsl-web-viewer recordings: the folder shown next to "saving to" (CSV per stream per take). - LabRecorder .xdf: Myo_EMG, Myo_IMU, Myo_Events, JackalState, JackalScan, JackalEvents, JackalCmd. - Armbands: stop each publisher, then myo_check.py --off on every Myo (no power button; otherwise it idles and drains overnight). It wakes again when plugged into USB, so charge them all before the next day. - In-session learning only, so no IRB. If any of this becomes research data, IRB applies.

items.title: 4. Troubleshooting (staff level)
items.text: Symptom Cause → fix Bridge: "address already in use" Something else holds port 8765 (on the dev Mac: the claude-science app, which also takes 8766). jackal-bridge --serve-site --open --port 8790. Clients then need --url ws://localhost:8790/cmd (or --bridge ws://localhost:8790). Panel grey on the GitHub Pages link Chrome's local-network prompt was denied, so re-allow it (lock icon → Site settings), or use --serve-site. Safari never connects from the GitHub link (it blocks https → ws://localhost with no prompt): always --serve-site. Bridge log: "refused a WebSocket from origin …" A page from an unknown site tried to connect (by design). A fork hosted elsewhere: --allow-origin https://yourorg.github.io. "Another sim tab is using the bridge" Two sim tabs; only one may connect. Close one, or press Connect in the one to keep. DEADMAN flicker The sender loop is slower than 4 Hz or blocks (slow classifier). Send at 20 Hz; resend the last value. High drop settings also cause it (expected). Commands ignored Another source is active (HUD/panel shows it). It must be silent for 1 s before another takes over. Myo: not found at all Turned off with --off, or a flat battery: plug into USB (that also wakes it). Myo: found but no connection Myo Connect still running, or the armband is connected to another laptop. On macOS: addresses from a plain scan are per-computer UUIDs; our scripts handle it. Pass the real MAC from myo_check.py step 2 to --addr. Myo: red "badly formed hexadecimal UUID" tracebacks Nearby phones / beacons advertising 32-bit IDs (bleak 0.20 bug). Our Myo scripts suppress it; harmless anyway. Myo: Python exits silently on the first scan (Mac) The terminal app has no Bluetooth permission (see checklist). Myo: very noisy EMG Fit (sizing clips, thickest part of the forearm), 2 min warm-up, re-sync. myo_lsl_publisher.py already uses the filtered mode. LSL streams not visible across two machines Campus wifi (eduroam) blocks multicast. Run everything on one laptop (the default), or add an lsl_api.cfg with [lab] KnownPeers = {192.168.x.a, 192.168.x.b} on both. pip/conda installs fail on an Apple-silicon Mac with an Intel Anaconda Works under Rosetta, but slow. Better: CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-arm64 conda env create -f environment.yml.

items.title: 5. Known limits
items.text:
• Physics mode (real skid-steer wheel friction) is not built yet (deferred). The robot is kinematic: it drives exactly as commanded and is stopped by obstacles.
  • The real-Jackal ROS adapter (brief M5) is not built.
  • Run logs live in the browser tab until downloaded; there is no server.

items.title: M0 Spike Findings: Jackal in browser MuJoCo
items.text: Status: M0 done. The Jackal MJCF loads in Chrome on a Mac, drives by keyboard in the L0 sandbox, and collides with the box without tunnelling. Evidence: web/tests/unit/sim.test.ts (physics in Node) and web/tests/e2e/m0.spec.ts (5/5 in Chrome 154 on macOS arm64).

items.title: Answers to the brief's open questions
items.text: Brief item Finding §4.1 official bindings @mujoco/mujoco 3.14.0 works, so the mjswan fallback isn't needed. loadMujoco() is the default export; models load via new mj.MjVFS() + vfs.addBuffer(name, bytes) + mj.MjModel.from_xml_string(xml, vfs). No FS juggling. <include file="jackal.xml"/> and meshdir resolve inside the VFS. Typed arrays (qpos, ctrl, geom_xpos…) are live views. data.contact is a copy: delete it (and each element) after use. §4.1 axis / quaternion glue None needed. three.js runs Z-up (camera.up = +z), and geoms are placed from MuJoCo's row-major geom_xmat + geom_xpos straight into a Matrix4. Meshes come from the compiled model (mesh_vert/mesh_face), so the browser loads no STLs separately. §4.2 Jackal model No Jackal in Menagerie. models/jackal/convert.py expands upstream jackal/jackal@noetic-devel (pinned 4ddf9b5) with pip xacro, after rewriting $(find …) and dropping the accessory includes (they pull other ROS packages). It then emits our own MJCF. Measured footprint 0.511 × 0.430 × 0.248 m, 18.4 kg, r = 0.098 m, track 0.3756 m, matching brief §4.2. Upstream license is BSD-3-Clause (copied to models/jackal/LICENSE). §3.2 limits jackal_control/config/control.yaml confirms max_velocity 2.0 m/s / 4.0 rad/s and cmd_vel_timeout: 0.25, the same as our deadman. The real robot's accel limits (20 m/s², 25 rad/s²) are far above our feel-tuned 2 / 6. §10.6 raycasting mj_ray and mj_multiRay are exposed in the JS typings, so the M2 lidar is unblocked. §10.7 load size mujoco.wasm is 10.3 MB raw / 2.5 MB gzip; JS 623 kB / 169 kB gzip; meshes 190 kB. Mac perf Real-time with large headroom: the Node physics tests run a 4 s drive in ~25 ms. Headless SwiftShader Chrome still holds 17 fps render with physics at real time.

items.title: Design decisions made during the spike
items.text:
• Deadman needs a braking limit. With symmetric 2 m/s² deceleration, 0.5 m/s → < 0.05 m/s takes 250 + 225 = 475 ms, which fails acceptance test 3 (400 ms). Added A_V_BRAKE = 4.0, A_W_BRAKE = 12.0 to limits.json: the robot brakes at twice its acceleration. E-stop is instant.
  • Kinematic base works as intended. Velocity actuators (kv 600, force-limited to 400 N) on slide x/y plus a force-limited hinge-yaw actuator. The robot stops exactly at box face minus half its length (x = 2.045 for a box face at 2.3), at both 1 and 2 m/s. Collision bits: robot/obstacles 2, floor 1.
  • Status semantics: deadman means "was told to move, then the link went quiet". A sender whose last command was a clean stop goes idle instead, so keyboard use doesn't flash DEADMAN on every key release.
  • The sim core is DOM-free (web/src/sim/*), and MuJoCo WASM runs in Node, so all physics acceptance checks are fast vitest tests. Playwright covers rendering, input and UI.

items.title: Toolchain gotchas
items.text:
1. Python on this Mac is x86_64 Anaconda (Rosetta), so the MuJoCo Python wheel refuses to import. Nothing depends on it: the model is validated by the WASM build in Node. The bridge (websockets, jsonschema, pylsl 1.18.5 with bundled liblsl 1.18) works fine under Rosetta.
  2. Playwright uses the installed Google Chrome (channel: 'chrome'). The bundled-Chromium download stalled, and real Chrome is what students use anyway. --use-gl=swiftshader (the telepresence repo's flag) no longer creates a WebGL context in Chrome 154; use --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader.
  3. Headless first frames take ~2 s (SwiftShader shader compile). Tests wait for __sim.time > 0.3.
  4. vite preview on Node 26 must bind 127.0.0.1 explicitly, or Chrome gets ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED on localhost (IPv6 vs IPv4).
  5. npm 11 blocks install scripts by default; esbuild works anyway via its platform optional dependency, so no approval is needed.

items.title: M1 findings (bridge)
items.text:
• Port 8765 can already be taken. On the dev Mac, claude-science listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 and
  • 8765 is also the port in the websockets library's own examples, so collisions on student laptops are plausible. The bridge now prints a clear fix (--port <PORT> + ?bridge=ws://localhost:<PORT>/sim). Open decision: keep 8765 (the brief's value), or freeze a less common default before teams start coding against protocol/v1.
  • Hidden tabs froze the sim (fixed). Chrome pauses requestAnimationFrame in hidden/background tabs, so with physics stepped from rAF, covering Chrome with a terminal froze the robot and the state stream (--loopback-test failed). Physics now steps from a dedicated-worker timer (web/src/sim/ticker.ts), which keeps firing in hidden tabs; rAF only renders. Verified: loopback PASS with the page hidden.
  • RTT is measured with a ping/pong on the 2 Hz bridge_status (tb → pong), not from cmd_echo_tb, because state is only sent every 50 ms and that echo overstates latency. Measured RTT on one laptop is about 1 ms.
  • pylsl 1.18.5 (bundled liblsl 1.18) works under Rosetta x86_64 Python, including the loopback JackalCmd / JackalAction round trip in bridge/tests/test_lsl.py and the e2e LSL spec.
  • Chrome logs every refused WebSocket attempt while no bridge runs (reconnect backoff 0.5 → 5 s). That is expected; the e2e "no console errors" check ignores just those lines.

items.title: Hosting findings (first GitHub Pages deploy)
items.text:
• Chrome on https://ahrtlab.github.io/Hackathon/ shows the Local Network Access prompt ("allow access to apps/devices on your local network") before connecting to ws://localhost. Students must click Allow.
  • Safari 26.6 blocks the https page → ws://localhost connection with no prompt. Verified on the dev Mac: from the Pages URL the bridge never saw a connection attempt; the same build served from http://localhost connected immediately. GitHub Pages therefore cannot support Safari.
  • Fix: jackal-bridge --serve-site. The bridge also serves the sim page at http://localhost:8765/Hackathon/ (same origin as the WebSocket, so there's no mixed content and no Chrome prompt). The page detects that it was served by the bridge (an injected <meta name="jackal-bridge">) and connects back to its own host. Site source order: --site-dir → repo web/dist → the download cache, filled from site.zip published with the site (about 2.6 MB download, 11 MB on disk). Verified in Safari with the real downloaded site.
  • The first Pages deploy showed a failed "deploy" job: GitHub started two runs 10 s apart (branch push plus enabling Pages) and the second collided with the first. Harmless; the first run is what's live.

items.title: M2 findings
items.text:
• mj_multiRay works in the JS bindings with IntBuffer / DoubleBuffer out-params (note GetView(), capital G; the package README says getView). Signature in 3.14: (m, d, pnt, vec, geomgroup[6], flg_static, bodyexclude, geomid, dist, normal, nray, cutoff). 180 beams take about 0.03 ms.
  • Courses are verified completable in Node: a TypeScript twin of autopilot_gates.py drives L1–L3 in real MuJoCo inside npm test (L1 18 s, L2 29 s, L3 20 s; 0 collisions, 0 missed gates), so a bad course edit fails fast. The Python autopilot does the same through the real bridge in Playwright.
  • HUD hardening: text that comes from team controllers (source, action) is now HTML-escaped before display.

items.title: Deployment: GitHub Actions from main
items.text:
• Publishing moved from a locally run scripts/deploy.sh (which pushed a built gh-pages branch) to .github/workflows/pages.yml: every push to main runs npm test, builds with SITE_BASE=/<repo>/, adds site.zip (for jackal-bridge --serve-site), and deploys. Pages source must be set to GitHub Actions. If it's set to "Deploy from a branch: main", GitHub renders the README as the site, which is exactly the "it's just READMEs" symptom we hit on 2026-10-15.
  • gh-pages is a record of what is live, not what Pages serves: after each successful deploy the workflow's record job commits the exact published files there (message: Deploy <sha> (main)).

items.title: Data
items.text:
AJ's recordings from 2026-10-22 are the dataset-2026-10-22 release (AJ-myo-lever-dataset.zip, about 3.7 MB). One driver, right arm, two wearings of the band.

Folder What it holds session1/, session2/ Six poses held for 2, 3 and 5 s: Myo_EMG (8 channels, 200 Hz) and Myo_IMU (10 channels, 50 Hz) per take results/runs/ The sim's official run CSVs: score, collisions, gates, smoothness, workload results/drives/ Every controller drive log: one row per 20 Hz command, with the EMG features the controller saw results/blind/ The keys for the blind lag-compensation test

File names give the pose:

Pose EMG label IMU label GO (arm forward, relaxed) rest neutral STOP (arm raised) arm_up arm_up LEFT / RIGHT (forearm rolled) roll_left / roll_right roll_left / roll_right REVERSE (arm tipped down) tip_down tip_down BRAKE (firm fist) forward brake

items.title: Use it
items.text:
python examples/myo_gestures.py drive <path>/session2 --mode lever   # drive with AJ's calibration
python examples/team_results.py <path>/results                       # recompute the results tables

In Python, gestures.load_recordings(folder, "Myo_EMG", labels, 8) from the repo's examples/ loads a folder. Split train and test by session or by person, never by window: windows from one take are near-copies of each other.

items.title: Other drivers
items.text: The four-driver comparison on the Results page also used recordings from Jose, Kiran and Xinyi. This site publishes only AJ's recordings and summary figures from the others.

items.title: Drive it
items.text:
You need the Myo armband, conda and Chrome. Quit Myo Connect first if it is running.

git clone https://github.com/ajbarea/Hackathon.git && cd Hackathon
conda env create -f environment.yml          # once, about 5 minutes
conda activate jackal                        # in every new terminal
python examples/lever.py <your name>

That one command:

  1. Connects to the Myo. On a Mac, allow Bluetooth for your terminal if asked.
  2. Calibrates you, the first time only (about 2.5 minutes). Put the band on snugly, on the thickest part of your forearm, and wait 2 minutes for it to warm up. Then hold six poses as it prompts you. Your calibration is saved in data/<your name>-lever.
  3. Opens the sim in your browser and drives. Pick a course (bottom right). Hold your arm forward and level for the countdown, then raise it once to start.
  4. Ctrl+C ends a drive. Then press Enter to drive again, r to recalibrate, t to tune the turns, or q to quit.

Next time, the same command skips straight to driving. Recalibrate whenever the band comes off.

items.title: How you drive
items.text:
Your arm The robot Forward, level Goes. Lower your arm to go faster Raised from the elbow Stops Rolled left or right Turns Tipped down Reverses Firm fist, held 0.4 s Brakes

Relaxing your hand never moves the robot, so driving is not tiring.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text:
What you see Fix CondaError: Run 'conda init' Run conda init zsh once (or conda init bash), then open a new terminal No Myo found, or stuck connecting Plug the Myo into USB for a few seconds to wake it, unplug it, and move it. Close Myo Connect Found once, then gone It fell asleep: unplug it, put it on and keep moving while it connects Still not found Another laptop may hold it: stop lever.py there, then run python examples/myo_check.py

More settings (--expo, --vmax, --no-assist, --no-lag-comp) and tuning are in examples/MYO_LEVER.md.

items.title: No armband?
items.text: Open the live sim and drive with W, A, S and D to see the courses. To try the signal pipeline, python examples/fake_myo_lsl.py publishes the same streams with synthetic data.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Myo armband ──BLE──► myo_lsl_publisher.py ──LSL──► Myo_EMG (8 ch, 200 Hz) + Myo_IMU (10 ch, 50 Hz)
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
                     myo_gestures.py drive --mode lever
                       IMU   → arm angle → speed and steering
                       EMG   → 16 features → LDA: fist or not → brake
                       lidar → slow before obstacles, gate nudge
                                                      │  (v, w) at 20 Hz
                                                      ▼
                          jackal-bridge ──WebSocket──► browser sim (scores every run)

items.title: Signals
items.text: Signal What we compute Drives Tilt (accelerometer, 50 Hz) Forearm height and roll from gravity, never yaw, so it does not drift Speed, steering, reverse Muscle (8 EMG channels, 200 Hz) Log RMS and log waveform length per channel, 200 ms windows Brake only Brake classifier Your fist against your other poses, by linear discriminant analysis Brake after a fist held 0.4 s Lidar (from the sim) Free space ahead and beside the robot Slow down, nudge off walls

items.title: Why the motion sensor steers
items.text: We started with five EMG gestures classified by LDA. On still poses it read 99 % of windows correctly. Hold a fist with the forearm rolled, which is what you do while steering, and it read 38 % correctly: rolling the arm moves the muscles under the electrodes. So the band's tilt sets speed and steering, and EMG decides only the brake.

items.title: Calibration
items.text: myo_gestures.py record prompts six poses (GO, STOP, LEFT, RIGHT, REVERSE, BRAKE), each held for 2, 3 and 5 s, and saves every take as CSV. The arm axes are learned from those takes, so the band works whichever way it is worn. Each drive starts by checking the straight pose still fits; if the band has moved, it refuses to start.

items.title: Assists
items.text:
• Lidar assist: slows before obstacles and keeps the robot off walls.
  • Gate assist (Xinyi): when you are already aimed within 20° of a gate, it steers toward the gate's centre by at most 0.3 rad/s. It never picks a gate for you; --no-gate switches it off.
  • Lag compensation: measures the command lag from the sim's echoes and drives the assist from the predicted pose. It switches on by itself when the link is slow.

items.title: Logs
items.text:
Every drive writes drives/drive_*.csv: one row per 20 Hz command, with the arm angles, the EMG features, the command sent and course progress.

Code: lever.py, myo_gestures.py, armdrive.py and gestures.py in examples/. Tests: pytest examples/tests.

items.title: Results
items.text: Everything here is recomputed from AJ's dataset with python examples/team_results.py <dataset>/results, and the neural-network tables with python examples/train_tcn.py.

items.title: Clean courses
items.text:
AJ's lever-mode drives, 2026-10-22. All 51 recorded runs completed with 0 missed gates.

Course Runs Median score Range Collisions L1 Gates 4 20.73 s 20.70 to 22.46 s 0 L2 Slalom 6 26.62 s 25.74 to 27.54 s 0 L3 Corridor + Dock 4 16.26 s 16.20 to 17.44 s 0

Score is time plus 5 s per collision and 10 s per missed gate; lower is better.

items.title: A slow, lossy link
items.text:
The judges also drove under a degraded link: 300 ms lag and 10 % of commands dropped. We ran a blind test of lag compensation: 8 sessions of 2 runs each on L1, with the condition hidden from the driver, compared session by session with an exact two-sided permutation test.

Measure On Off p Score 21.66 s 22.51 s 0.57 Steering jerkiness 0.66 rad/s² 0.74 rad/s² 0.63 Workload (NASA-RTLX, 0 to 100) 43.4 50.4 0.26 Collisions (total) 0 2

Every median favours it, and none of the differences is significant. We keep it on because it did no measurable harm; we cannot claim it helps.

items.title: A neural network against the simple model
items.text:
Four drivers (AJ, Jose, Kiran, Xinyi), 3 seeds per held-out driver. A causal temporal convolutional network (TCN) on the raw signal, against the controller's linear discriminant (LDA) on 16 features. Accuracy over six poses; chance is 0.17. Each cell is the median across drivers, range in brackets.

Test TCN LDA Your own calibration 0.68 (0.45 to 0.89) 0.85 (0.76 to 0.88) A driver it never saw, each scaled by their own calibration 0.33 (0.23 to 0.38) 0.32 (0.29 to 0.34)

The second row is the TCN without gain augmentation, its better setting for a new driver. On each person's own data the LDA won for 3 of 4 drivers, and neither model generalises well to someone new. With 2.5 minutes of data per person the simple model is the right choice, and in lever mode EMG decides only the brake, where the personal LDA made no false fires and no misses on held-out takes.

Full tables, with and without gain augmentation: examples/TCN.md.

items.title: The gate assist
items.text: Six scripted off-line approaches to L1's first gate, through the real sim with the controller's assist code: 2 of 6 passed the gate with the assist, 0 of 6 without, and 0 collisions either way (gate-trial.json).
